suite_baseline.reconciliation: As recorded in parity/control-plane.ledger.json: 2194 collected + 5 modules skipped at collection time = 2199. Unchanged by this belt.

subsystem.name: measurement
subsystem.note: The G6 harness, interlock tests/measurement, 14 files. One ledger per source file. latency is the fourth file of this lane and the first to consume another measurement module's output: censoring is windows.ts's decision and arrives here already made, which is why a censored episode is excluded from the distribution rather than re-judged.

systematic_mappings.from: frozen dataclasses with tuple fields and Mapping returns
systematic_mappings.to: frozen classes whose collections go through frozenList / readOnlyMap (src/measurement/immutable.ts)
systematic_mappings.why: The convention established in the false-termination belt (D-0105's sibling reasoning): TypeScript's readonly is erased at runtime and Object.freeze is shallow, so the source's runtime immutability has to be built. Distribution, ShadowReference, ShadowSource, IngestionLag, ClassLatency and LatencyReport are all frozen. Changes how a case spells a construction, never what it asserts.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that constructs or reads a report object

systematic_mappings.from: Mapping[str, int] detections, Mapping[str, tuple[int, ...]] samples
systematic_mappings.why: D-0105: the keys are episode ids and incident classes that arrive from a caller's selection, so a plain object's prototype chain could answer a lookup. Applied uniformly.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that supplies detections or shadow samples

systematic_mappings.to: isAscii() from src/measurement/format.ts, and a split-based occurrence count
systematic_mappings.why: Neither exists in JavaScript. isAscii iterates code points (D-0006); the occurrence count is non-overlapping, which is what Python's str.count is.

systematic_mappings.to: an explicit length assertion followed by an index
systematic_mappings.why: Python's unpack asserts exactly-one as a side effect of binding. The target asserts the length first so that a report with two classes fails on the count rather than on a later field, which is the same claim made visible.
systematic_mappings.affects: the entries that read a single class off a report

ids: test/measurement/latency.test.ts::the report itself > percentiles are ceil-rank, on a sample where floor would differ (target-only)
test/measurement/latency.test.ts::the report itself > a class present in the shadow source with an EMPTY sample is absent for it (target-only)
test/measurement/latency.test.ts::the report itself > classes are reported in first-seen order, not sorted (target-only)
target_only_tests.note: Target-only tests translate no source case and are NOT counted as ported coverage. All three close INHERITED blind spots found by a 22-mutation sweep and then confirmed against interlock 65f36c5 -- in each case the source's own suite cannot tell the mutated module from the real one either. Production behaviour is unchanged; these add coverage, not behaviour. This module has no seam (nothing in it is monkeypatched by the source) and renders no figure through D-0104's formatter, so neither of those liveness obligations applies.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The v1 shadow distribution is a caller-supplied input, never read from this database, so nothing in the harness verifies that the samples handed in are really v1's both-bucket episodes for that class.
inherited_limitations.note: Deliberate upstream and structural rather than an omission: interlock D-0013 makes a run row's existence the assertion that the run is Interlock-owned, so there is no ownership column a v1 episode could be read out of. The obligation the module CAN discharge -- that a class is never rendered against the budget alone, and that an empty per-class sample becomes a stated absence rather than a zero -- is discharged in the type.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: upstream, and only alongside a v1 store the harness could read directly.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: A shadow comparison is never turned into a verdict: the report prints both references and says nothing about whether the class passed.
inherited_limitations.note: interlock Q-0005 is open and measurement-harness.md section 5 says a harness that emitted a verdict would be answering it by inertia. Reproduced exactly, and recorded here so the absence is not mistaken for an unfinished feature.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere until Q-0005 is decided upstream.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: Interlock's latency suite cannot distinguish a ceil-rank percentile from a floor-rank one, cannot distinguish an empty per-class shadow sample from a missing one, and does not assert the order classes are reported in.
inherited_limitations.note: Three blind spots found by a mutation sweep on the port and then verified against interlock 65f36c5. The port reproduces the production behaviour exactly and does not change it; it adds three target-only tests so the properties stop being unguarded on this side. Disclosed rather than fixed upstream because interlock#74 acceptance criterion 5 requires known limitations to stay disclosed, and a test added to interlock is a change to the other side of the comparison.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: upstream, as the same three cases added to interlock's tests/measurement/test_latency.py.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The ShadowReference constructor validates only the distribution for a SHADOW_PRESENT reference, not bothBucketCount. A caller constructing one directly with a distribution and a null count is accepted, and the renderer then prints 'over null both-bucket episode(s)'.
inherited_limitations.note: Raised by the codex review gate on this PR as a P2. Verified empirically against interlock 65f36c5: ShadowReference(status='present', distribution=..., both_bucket_count=None, reason=None) is accepted by __post_init__ -- which checks only `distribution is None` for the present state -- and render_latency_report emits 'over None both-bucket episode(s)'. NOT fixed here: adding the check would make continuo refuse an input interlock accepts, which is a silent behavioural divergence in a parity port. Handled under the precedent the operator set for action_id escaping on 2026-08-22: reproduce and disclose, do not repair one side alone. Unreachable through the module's own API -- ShadowReference.present always supplies the count, and forClass is the only internal caller -- so this is a hand-constructed state, which is exactly why the source's own invariant stops where it does. One knock-on worth naming for the future CLI oracle face: in that unreachable state the two runtimes render different TEXT ('None' against 'null'), because each prints its own spelling of the absent value. That is a faithful consequence rather than a second defect, but a CLI comparison driven into this state would report it as a mismatch.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: upstream, as a __post_init__ that also requires both_bucket_count for the present state -- and then in continuo in the same change, so the two keep accepting the same inputs.

entries.reason: Python enforces the exclusive-or in `__post_init__`, which runs for a dataclass built by hand as well as through the two classmethods. TypeScript has no equivalent hook, so the validation lives in the constructor and the constructor is public -- which is what the source case needs, since it builds four malformed values directly and asserts each refuses. Same four constructions, same refusal type, same coverage; only the place the invariant is written differs.

mutation_sweep.ran: 22 mutations, one per property the ported cases claim to pin, 2026-08-22

survivors.mutation: nearestRank uses Math.floor instead of Math.ceil
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Every sample interlock's suite uses is one where the two rules coincide: n=10 (ceil and floor of both 0.5n and 0.9n are equal), n=1, and n=3 with three IDENTICAL values. The new case uses three DISTINCT values, where ceil(0.5*3)=2 and floor=1.

survivors.mutation: ShadowSource.forClass treats an empty sample list as present rather than absent
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported case supplies a source holding a DIFFERENT class, so the lookup misses and returns undefined; the branch where the class is present with an empty list is never taken. Interlock's `if not samples:` covers both and its one test exercises only the missing key. The distinction is the one the module comment names: an empty distribution renders as 'v1: count 0' and reads as no regression.

survivors.mutation: measureLatency sorts the class list instead of keeping first-seen order
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The two-class ported case counts headings rather than reading the order, and interlock never asserts class order anywhere. First-seen order is a D-0040 byte-reproducibility claim, so the new case uses a fixture where sorted and first-seen differ ('relay_gap' sorts before 'session_no_evidence' while the episodes present the latter first).
